cause: LINE ENDINGS, AND NOTHING ELSE. instrument_revision.sha256_of hashes RAW working-tree bytes and never normalizes, by the deliberate rule in docs/hash_basis_policy.md, so the HEAD of the revision chain is pinned to working-tree digests while a SUPERSEDED link is proved from COMMITTED blobs by _check_historical_link. Those two bases agree only while the working tree is byte-identical to its commit. This repository declares '* text=auto eol=lf' in .gitattributes, so git normalizes CRLF to LF on commit and reports the working-tree file as UNCHANGED -- git status, git diff and git diff --check all stay silent -- while the raw bytes hash differently. src/iqa_soa/experiment/confirmatory_registration.py was written into the working tree with CRLF on 3875 of its 3912 newlines, so the digest captured for it, and the tree digest computed over it, describe bytes no commit can hold. The record was correct about WHAT changed and WHY; it captured the affected file's digest on the wrong byte basis. docs/hash_basis_policy.md section 6.1 states the rule that was missed: verify checkout conformance -- no CRLF in the working-tree bytes -- BEFORE generating a frozen artifact. Section 6.3 states the repair: never edit a recorded digest to make a check pass; record the difference in a new amendment, which is what this record is.
corrected_scope: EXACTLY two values are superseded: current_instrument.src_iqa_soa_tree, and the single per-file SHA-256 named in affected_files. Every other value in the corrected record -- its parent commit, its previous_instrument block, its approved change set, every scientific reason, every benchmark hash, every version constant and every scientific statement -- stands exactly as written and is unchanged by this correction. The corrected record's previous_instrument block is reproduced here verbatim because the Phase-O hand-off it names was never defective: it is provable from committed bytes at its own parent commit today.

It is retained as HISTORICAL EVIDENCE OF THE DEFECT, which is why it was not rewritten to make its own hashes pass.
